answer: Pay agents on a glacier schedule: earnings vest slowly over many epochs, so a Sybil farm must keep every fake alive and working long before it profits. Standing also needs a liveness pulse — a signed proof from a sequential computation that cannot run in parallel, so one operator cannot pulse dozens of identities at once. Identities whose pulses arrive in lockstep, or that earn without ever pulsing, are quarantined as hollow shells: vested funds freeze and sponsors' bonds are slashed. One fake is cheap; a hundred pulsing on time through glacier-long vesting costs more than the work pays.
